docs.title: Welcome
docs.text: The denguedasets package provide a curated collection of open-access dengue fever surveillance and climate datasets for epidemiological research and machine learning. Includes surveillance records, climatic co-variates, and mortality indicators from Bangladesh, the Philippines, Taiwan, Sri Lanka, Brazil, Colombia, Pakistan, India, Peru, Indonesia, and Sierra Leone, spanning case counts, deaths, case-fatality rates, and associated meteorological variables (temperature, humidity, precipitation) suitable for spatiotemporal analysis, outbreak prediction, machine learning, and time-series modeling from Kaggle.

docs.title: Philosophy
docs.text:
The authors' vision is to create data packages, functions, or a combination of both in Julia, R, and Python, contributing to the interoperability of algorithms and data to transform the information into decisions that help solve specific problems.

In the case of data packages, the authors' vision is to create specialized packages focused on specific topics and subtopics. Instead of searching through multiple diverse and heterogeneous sources, users can access all these interesting datasets in a single package.

Specifically, in the case of the denguedasets package, each included dataset is specialized in dengue fever, providing a valuable source of information for academics, data scientists, statisticians, modelers, university professors, or students interested in working with this combination of topics.

docs.title: From  PyPI
docs.text:
The easiest way to install the denguedatasets package is directlty from PyPI:

pip install denguedatasets

docs.title: From GitHub
docs.text:
To get the latest development version with newest features and bugs fixes is directlty from GitHub:

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Initial release of denguedatasets.
  • 17 curated dengue surveillance and climate datasets from 11 countries: Bangladesh, Brazil, Colombia, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, Peru, Philippines, Sierra Leone, Sri Lanka, and Taiwan.
  • list_datasets() to list all available dataset keys.
  • dataset_info() to inspect metadata (source, license, description) before loading.
  • load_dataset() to load any dataset as a pandas DataFrame, with support for all pandas.read_csv keyword arguments.
  • describe() to generate summary statistics for any dataset.
  • Structured metadata for each dataset documented in the Datasets Catalog.

docs.title: Datasets included in denguedatasets
docs.text: This file documents the origin and license of each dataset included in the denguedatasets Python package.

docs.title: dengue_bangladesh
docs.text: Source: Kaggle URL: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/kawsarahmad/dengue-dataset-bangladesh Title: Dengue Dataset of Bangladesh. Unraveling Dengue: Analyzing and Mapping Affected Areas in Bangladesh for Target License: CC BY 4.0 Original Name: dataset.csv Final Name: dengue_bangladesh.csv Description: This dataset presents real-world data collected through surveys conducted in the Dhaka region of Bangladesh. It focuses on understanding the prevalence and characteristics of the Dengue fever phenomenon, a significant public health concern in the area. The dataset is updated monthly to reflect the evolving nature of the Dengue outbreak.

docs.title: dengue_bangladesh_mortality
docs.text: Source: Kaggle URL: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/gazijahin/climatic-influence-on-dengue-mortality-2000-2024 Title: Climatic Influence on Dengue Mortality (2000-2024). Effects of climatic factors for increasing the risk of Dengue cases License: MIT Original Name: Climatic_Influence_on_Dengue_Mortality.csv Final Name: dengue_bangladesh_mortality.csv Description: This dataset explores the spatio-temporal interaction between climate variability and dengue outbreaks across six divisions of Bangladesh from 2000 to 2024. It connects meteorological parameters with epidemiological indicators (cases, deaths, and case-fatality rate) to uncover how changing weather patterns influence dengue mortality.

docs.title: dengue_philippines
docs.text: Source: Kaggle URL: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/vincentgupo/dengue-cases-in-the-philippines Title: Philippines Dengue Cases 2016-2020 License: CC0: Public Domain Original Name: ph_dengue_cases2016-2020.csv Final Name: dengue_philippines.csv Description: Data set contains the recorded number of dengue cases per region of the Philippines from year 2016 to 2020. It can be used to find trends about the disease as well as spatiotemporal analysis that can result into data-driven solution about the trends of the desease for the past 5 years.

docs.title: dengue_taiwan
docs.text: Source: Kaggle URL: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/taweilo/taiwan-dengue-daily-confirmed-cases-1998-2024 Title: Taiwan Dengue Cases 1998-2024. Daily and Regional Confirmed Cases of Dengue from 1998 to 2024 License: CC0: Public Domain Original Name: Dengue_Daily_EN.csv Final Name: dengue_taiwan.csv Description: The dataset contains detailed information on dengue fever cases since 1998, encompassing various aspects such as dates, geographical locations, and serotype details. This data can be leveraged to analyze temporal trends, spatial distribution, and the serotype of dengue cases. It is valuable for understanding the disease's progression, its impact across different regions, and the effectiveness of intervention measures over time.

docs.title: dengue_brazil
docs.text: Source: Kaggle URL: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/raomuhammadsaeedali/brazil-dengue-dataset-2000-2019 Title: Brazil Dengue Dataset 2000-2019. Brazil Dengue Dataset offers insights into geography, environment, and disease. License: GPL 2 Original Name: data_2000_2019.csv Final Name: dengue_brazil.csv Description: The dataset supplied comprises a comprehensive collection of information pertaining to numerous geographical and environmental characteristics across microregions in Brazil from 2000 to 2019. Microregion codes and names, mesoregion codes and names, state codes and names, region codes and names, biome codes and names, ecozone codes and names, climate regimes, months, years, times, dengue cases, population estimates, population density, maximum and minimum temperatures, Palmer's drought severity index, urban population percentages, access to water network percentages, and reported water shortage frequency are all included in the dataset. This information is linked to individual microregions and provides insights into population dynamics, climatic patterns, urbanization trends, water resources, and disease occurrences.

docs.text: Source: Kaggle URL: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/raomuhammadsaeedali/brazil-dengue-dataset-2000-2019 Title: Brazil Dengue Dataset 2000-2019 — Data Dictionary License: GPL 2 Original Name: data_desc.csv Final Name: dengue_brazil_labels.csv Description: Data dictionary/variable-label reference table accompanying the Brazil Dengue Dataset 2000-2019, documenting field names, codes, and descriptions used across microregion, mesoregion, state, region, biome, and ecozone identifiers, as well as climatic and demographic variables in the main dataset.

docs.title: denguedatasets – Examples
docs.text: This page provides practical examples of using denguedatasets for data analysis and exploration.

docs.title: Example 1: Loading and Exploring a Dataset
docs.text:
Learn how to load a dataset and perform basic exploration.

import denguedatasets as dd

# Load the dengue cases of Colombia
den_col = dd.load_dataset("dengue_colombia")
# Display first few rows
print(den_col.head())
# Check dataset shape
print(f"\nDataset shape: {den_col.shape}")
# View column names
print(f"\nColumns: {list(den_col.columns)}")
# Get summary statistics
print("\nSummary statistics:")
print(den_col.describe())
# Check for missing values
print("\nMissing values:")
print(den_col.isnull().sum())

import denguedatasets as dd

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide will help you install denguedatasets and load your first dengue dataset in a few minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Python 3.8 or higher. pandas (installed automatically with denguedatasets). Installation

From PyPI (Recommended)

The easiest way to install the package is directly from the Python Package Index:

pip install denguedatasets

From GitHub

If you want the latest development version, you can install it directly from the repository:

pip install git+https://github.com/fdzul/denguedatasets-py

docs.title: 1. Your First Dataset
docs.text:
Once installed, using the package is straightforward. Follow these three steps:

  1. Import the package
import denguedatasets as dd

docs.title: 2. See what is available
docs.text:
List all datasets included in the package to find the key you need:

print(dd.list_datasets())

docs.title: 3. Load and analyze
docs.text:
Load the dataset into a pandas DataFrame and start working:

# Load Taiwan dengue data
df = dd.load_dataset("dengue_taiwan")

# Display the first 5 rows
print(df.head())

# Check the shape of the data
print(f"Rows: {df.shape[0]}, Columns: {df.shape[1]}")
